\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Two Function}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Reverse.TwoFunction
\section{Overview}
The extended power means are monotone in their finite exponent up to one. Two-function reverse hypercontractivity gives lower bounds for correlated pairings of nonnegative cube functions.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity in the exponent]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_exponent_mono}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{7}
Let $a\le b\le1$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $M_a(f)\le M_b(f)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Two-function reverse hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_bonami_beckner_two_function}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_exponent_mono, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_bonami_beckner, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_holder, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct_comm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint}
\difficulty{6}
Let $p,q<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le(1-p)(1-q)$. For all $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$, uniform expectation satisfies $\E[fT_\rho g]\ge M_p(f)M_q(g)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}
